findings.title: Money requested before any viewing
findings.detail: The agent asks for money before you have seen the property in person. Paying before a viewing is the most common way students lose a deposit.

evidence.quote: The owner Mira Vale is abroad. You cannot view until you pay. Buy GBP 1500 in prepaid gift cards and send the redemption codes by 16 November 2026 at 18:00, or I will give the room to someone else.

findings.title: Untraceable payment method requested
findings.detail: Money transfer services, gift cards, pre-paid cards and crypto cannot be traced or refunded. Genuine landlords and agencies do not take rent or deposits this way.

evidence.quote: Buy GBP 1500 in prepaid gift cards and send the redemption codes by 16 November 2026 at 18:00, or I will give the room to someone else.

findings.title: Deposit is within the amount cap
findings.detail: This amount check does not verify deposit protection or authenticity. Annual rent GBP 15600; cap = 15600 / 52 * 5 (GBP 1500.00 rounded down to pennies); requested GBP 1500. Importance: 85/100. Conditional: Confirm that the rented property is in England. Confirm this is an ordinary private tenancy, not an excluded arrangement. Confirm that rent and deposit cover the same whole tenancy. The cap arithmetic holds: rent of GBP 1300 a month is GBP 15,600 a year, five weeks of that is GBP 1,500.00, and the stated deposit is GBP 1,500. So the amount is at, not above, the cap, and no breach is shown. The conclusion stays conditional because jurisdiction and tenancy type are unknown in the context. Nothing in the contract confirms the property is in England or that this is an ordinary covered private tenancy. It also does not confirm that the rent and deposit cover the same whole tenancy. The Rent and Tenancy deposit clauses (s5, s6) support the figures but not these scope facts. No quoted counter-evidence defeats the issue. This amount check says nothing about deposit protection or authenticity. Sources: https://www.gov.uk/guidance/tenant-fees-act-2019-guidance-for-tenants

questions: Is this a private tenancy in England with the landlord living elsewhere?
What rent period and tenancy does the deposit cover, and can the amount be revised?

findings.title: Wording that hides a plain meaning
findings.detail: Calling gift card codes a 'reservation system' makes a payment sound like an official process; the plain version is that you are being asked to hand over gift card codes as payment.

evidence.quote: The codes are our reservation system.

findings.title: What the messages actually state
findings.detail: • The student asks to view Flat 2, 20 Example Mews on 15 November 2026 at 16:00 before paying. • The owner, Mira Vale, is said to be abroad. • No viewing is possible until payment is made. • Payment is requested as GBP 1500 in prepaid gift cards, with the redemption codes sent to the agent. • The deadline for sending the codes is 16 November 2026 at 18:00. • The student says the contract names Mira Vale and lists Rowan Pike as managing agent. • The agent says no bank transfer alternative is available. • The agent says no viewing will happen before the codes arrive.

findings.title: Rent above the area average
findings.detail: £1,300 a month against roughly £950 for a room in W12 (approximate area figure): about 37% higher. Not a scam sign, but worth knowing.
